title: Bounded site transport of closed exceptional Tate objects
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $1\le m\le n$. Set $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^n)$, $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^m)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], write $a_Y:Y	o s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $F_{Y,R}=Ra_{Y,R!}\dashv G_{Y,R}=a_{Y,R}^{	imes}$, $\omega_{Y,R}=G_{Y,R}R_s$, and $\varepsilon_{Y,R}:F_{Y,R}\omega_{Y,R}	o R_s$, for $R=A,B$, on ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $T_Y=-\otimes_A^LB$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and denote the canonical compact-support coefficient comparison by $c_{Y,K}:T_sF_{Y,A}K	o F_{Y,B}T_YK$ [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. Here bounded constructible finite-Tor means constructible cohomology, zero outside a finite interval, and integers $a\le b$ such that tensoring with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Let $i:Y\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf A^r_k$ be closed, with $Y$ affine, and set $M=\omega_{P,A}$, $M_B=T_PM$, $N=I_AM$, where $I_R=Ri^!_{\mathrm{et},R}$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. Put $S_{W,R}=
u_W^*$ and $U_{W,R}=R
u_{W,*}$ for etale/pro-etale comparison, $W=Y,P$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $J_R=S_{Y,R}I_RU_{P,R}$ carry the bounded-below etale-origin adjunction for the identity-open compactification [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. For $W=Y,P$, let $T_W^{\mathrm{pro}}=-\otimes_A^LB$ on the pro-etale site, and let $e_{R,H}:i^{\mathrm{et}}_{R*}I_RH	o H$ be the ordinary closed exceptional counit. There are natural isomorphisms of actual derived $B$-module sheaves $t_{W,K}:S_{W,B}(T_WK)\cong T_W^{\mathrm{pro}}S_{W,A}K$. The specified comparison unit $\eta_{R,H}:H\cong U_{P,R}S_{P,R}H$ gives $\alpha_{R,H}=S_{Y,R}I_R(\eta_{R,H}):S_{Y,R}I_RH\cong J_RS_{P,R}H$, for $(R,H)=(A,M),(B,M_B)$. The objects $M,N,M_B,I_BM_B$ are bounded constructible finite-Tor on the etale sites, and their comparison pullbacks, including $J_AS_{P,A}M$, have this property on the pro-etale sites. The canonical bounded-below direct-image comparison $\delta_{R,L}:S_{P,R}i^{\mathrm{et}}_{R*}L\cong Ri^{\mathrm{pro}}_{R*}S_{Y,R}L$ is the inverse compact-support site comparison for the identity-open compactification [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate, lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. With $E$ the specified transported exceptional counit, one has $E_{R,S_{P,R}H}\circ Ri^{\mathrm{pro}}_{R*}(\alpha_{R,H})\circ\delta_{R,I_RH}=S_{P,R}(e_{R,H})$. The isomorphisms use only bounded-below etale-origin Hom bijections, including when $Y$ is empty.

proof.text: Use closedDualizingEtaleFiniteness for the four ordinary bounded constructible finite-Tor objects. Extract a lower bound from bounded constructibility for every ordinary input and exceptional image.
The actual coefficient comparison pbcComparisonReductionMap is invertible by its existing proved theorem, on every scheme, hence on Y and P.

Apply the existing generic torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory to each ordinary Tor interval. The bounded-constructible image property follows by ObjectProperty.prop_map_obj. These give the four pro-etale finiteness assertions.

Invert the actual comparison unit on the bounded-below H, and apply I and S to obtain alpha. Use asIso alpha to retain the explicit origin IH for JSH; transport boundedness, constructible-image membership and Tor amplitude across this isomorphism.

Use closedIdentityOpenHomNormalization at the zero ordinary object and its zero exceptional image. Its direct-image clause is independent of that object and gives exactly dualizingClosedSiteDirectImage at both positive coefficient levels. The named identity-open isomorphisms in the two modules are definitionally the same.

Expand specifiedExceptionalHomEquiv at the retained origin (IH,asIso alpha). Its inverse identity equals pro-etale compact support of alpha inverse, followed by fixedCompactSupportComparisonIso at IH and S of the ordinary counit: apply injectivity of the equivalence, cancel the origin maps and comparison, use unit naturality at the ordinary counit, and ordinary adjunction naturality with beta(counit)=identity. After precomposition with the inverse canonical compact-support comparison and pro-etale compact support of alpha, cancel alpha and identify the fixed comparison with the canonical one by compactSupportComparisonNormalization. This proves the prescribed counit equation with the actual witness, at A and B.
